paragraphs.heading: Computational FSI simulations: scope and objectives
paragraphs.purpose: State the overall computational strategy: use a previously validated cost‑effective pulsatile FSI pipeline to generate a large, time‑resolved dataset for two idealized plaque phenotypes (LAP, CP) to support VI development and sensitivity analysis.
must_not_claim: that the cost‑effective FSI method is newly developed or validated here (this work only reuses a prior validated tool)
any results or sensitivity findings

paragraphs.purpose: Describe the PDE/constitutive physics and numerical coupling used in the FSI solver: incompressible 3D Navier–Stokes (Newtonian fluid) + finite‑deformation quasi‑static solid (Neo‑Hookean / linear elastic), partitioned strong coupling, and time integration.
must_not_claim: that alternative continuum constitutive models (e.g., anisotropic, viscoelastic) were used
any performance/results (e.g., accuracy metrics) of the solver beyond numerical settings

paragraphs.heading: Numerical implementation and verification
paragraphs.purpose: Specify key numerical parameters and verification checks: time stepping (BDF2, Δt=0.5 ms, 1600 steps/cycle, 3 cycles to periodic steady state), partitioned fixed‑point residual tolerance, mesh and time‑step independence study and mesh sizes.
must_not_claim: that extensive new solver verification/validation against experimental data is performed here
that mesh/time independence implies zero numerical error

paragraphs.heading: Geometry, material models and parameter ranges
paragraphs.purpose: Describe the idealized plaque geometries (LAP: 3 domains; CP: 4 domains), the material constitutive assumptions (Neo‑Hookean nearly incompressible for vessel and fibrous cap; linear elastic for core and calcification), and the literature‑based parameter ranges used for sampling.
must_not_claim: that the chosen geometries capture the full patient‑specific variability
that more complex material behaviours (anisotropy, viscoelasticity) were modelled

paragraphs.purpose: Explain the input design‑space sampling and case generation: 1,000 parameter sets sampling morphology, hemodynamics and materials (LHS/uniform ranges) as the basis for the FSI runs and downstream surrogates.
must_not_claim: that the design space exhaustively covers all physiologic conditions
that sampling replaced any targeted clinical cohort sampling

paragraphs.heading: Output processing and candidate VI computation
paragraphs.purpose: Define the computed outputs from each FSI case (peak PSS, pulsatile amplitude ΔPSS spherical average, FFR surrogate, rupture‑location index) and describe how six candidate VIs were formed (stress: peak PSS and ΔPSS × strength normalizations E_fc^α for α scenarios).
must_not_claim: that these outputs are clinical endpoints (no patient outcome data used)
that the candidate VI definitions are the only possible definitions

paragraphs.heading: Clinical sign‑consistency screening of VI candidates
paragraphs.purpose: Describe the screening procedure that scores the six candidate VIs against seven established clinical high‑risk plaque criteria via sign‑consistency (1/0) with 95% BCa bootstrap CIs (1,000 resamples) to select final VIs for surrogate/GSA.
must_not_claim: that screening substitutes for outcome‑based clinical validation
that bootstrap CIs eliminate all sampling uncertainty

paragraphs.heading: Gaussian process surrogate training
paragraphs.purpose: Give the surrogate modelling workflow: ARD Matérn 5/2 + white‑noise kernel GPR, input z‑score normalization and output standardization, hyperparameter optimization with L‑BFGS‑B and 20 restarts, and 5‑fold cross‑validation reporting and effective training set sizes (LAP 784 / CP 727).
must_not_claim: that the surrogate perfectly reproduces the FSI model without error
any clinical diagnostic claims based solely on the surrogate

paragraphs.heading: Global sensitivity analysis on the surrogate
paragraphs.purpose: Describe the Saltelli sampling and Sobol index estimation protocol executed on the trained GPR surrogate (~15,000 base samples), with computation of first‑order (S1) and total (ST) indices at group (morphology/hemodynamics/materials) and parameter levels and convergence checks.
must_not_claim: that surrogate‑based Sobol indices are identical to indices computed from the raw FSI model without approximation
that Sobol analysis determines causation rather than variance attribution

paragraphs.heading: Validation of simulation outputs
paragraphs.purpose: Establish face validity of the pulsatile FSI outputs by reporting that simulated PSS, FFR and rupture-location trends are consistent with prior literature and that the simulation pipeline produced stable, interpretable outputs for downstream analysis.
must_not_claim: Do not claim clinical outcome prediction or patient-specific prognostic validity from these simulation-only comparisons
Do not assert that the cost-effective FSI method is newly validated here (method/tool is cited from prior work)

paragraphs.purpose: Report the candidate vulnerability-index (VI) screening against seven established clinical high‑risk plaque criteria and identify which candidates fully satisfy those criteria.
must_not_claim: Do not claim these VIs are clinically validated with patient outcome data
Do not claim the screening substitutes for prospective clinical validation

paragraphs.purpose: Present surrogate-evaluated diagnostic separation for the selected VI(s) (synthetic high-risk label), giving ROC AUC and operating-point metrics to quantify potential discriminative utility.
must_not_claim: Do not claim real-world diagnostic performance or clinical utility beyond the synthetic-label evaluation
Do not imply prospective patient-level validation has been performed

paragraphs.heading: Global sensitivity: material dominance
paragraphs.purpose: Summarize group-level Sobol sensitivity analysis showing that the material-property group explains the largest fraction of VI variance (Material > Hemodynamics > Morphology) and quantify the group-level indices supporting the material-dominant conclusion.
must_not_claim: Do not claim that sensitivity results uniformly generalize to all patient geometries beyond the two phenotypes studied (LAP, CP)
Do not assert causal mechanistic pathways beyond variance attribution

paragraphs.purpose: Report individual-parameter Sobol indices that rank the top contributors to VI variability (identifying E_vessel, E_fc, SBP, PP) and give representative first-order S1 values (e.g., E_fc S1 ≈ 0.55 for LAP·VI2).
must_not_claim: Do not claim these parameter rankings are exhaustive for all physiologic ranges not sampled in the design space
Do not claim that changing one parameter in isolation will deterministically change rupture events in patients

paragraphs.heading: Interpretation of stress metric and strength normalization
paragraphs.purpose: Demonstrate that ΔPSS (pulsatile amplitude) yields better alignment with clinical high‑risk features than peak PSS and that normalizing stress by fibrous-cap strength (E_fc^α) materially affects VI behavior, motivating the selected VI definitions (VI1, VI2).
must_not_claim: Do not claim that the chosen α values (0.5, 1.0) exhaustively represent the true biological scaling of cap strength
Do not claim that stress-only metrics are universally invalid in all contexts without further study

paragraphs.heading: Key findings
paragraphs.purpose: Summarize the study's principal results succinctly, linking the primary contributions (VI definition, ΔPSS relevance, and material dominance) to evidence produced.
must_not_claim: That the selected VIs have been prospectively validated on patient outcome data
That causation (e.g., changing E_fc will necessarily change clinical rupture rates) has been established

paragraphs.heading: Interpreting stress: ΔPSS and the need for pulsatile FSI
paragraphs.purpose: Explain why pulsatile amplitude (ΔPSS) is a more appropriate stress metric than instantaneous peak PSS, justify the fatigue perspective, and state the methodological implication that time-resolved FSI is required to compute ΔPSS.
must_not_claim: That quasi-static or steady simulations are never useful for any plaque assessment
That ΔPSS fully captures all mechanisms of plaque failure (e.g., biochemical/biological factors)

paragraphs.heading: Strength-normalization of VIs and sensitivity to exponent α
paragraphs.purpose: Discuss the rationale and empirical support for normalizing stress by fibrous-cap strength (E_fc^α), report how different α choices change VI behavior, and link this to the candidate-VI screening that selected VI1 and VI2.
must_not_claim: That the simple E_fc^α model fully represents patient-specific strength or fracture mechanics
That the chosen α values are definitive for all contexts without further empirical validation

paragraphs.heading: Clinical and methodological implications of material dominance
paragraphs.purpose: Interpret group- and parameter-level Sobol results to explain how material properties dominate VI variability and what this implies for clinical measurement priorities and mechanistic focus.
must_not_claim: That imaging morphology measurements (e.g., plaque shape) are clinically useless
That this dominance directly implies immediate changes in clinical management without prospective validation

paragraphs.heading: Surrogate modelling, Sobol GSA and methodological advantages
paragraphs.purpose: Explain why GPR surrogates plus Saltelli/Sobol analysis enabled the global sensitivity study at reasonable cost, summarize surrogate performance and convergence checks, and note practical implications for future computational studies.
must_not_claim: That surrogate-based Sobol results are exact replacements for exhaustive full-FSI sampling without approximation error
That the surrogate removes the need for any FSI simulations (original FSI data remain necessary)

paragraphs.heading: Limitations and future work
paragraphs.purpose: List the main limitations of the computational study (idealized geometry, uniform cap thickness, material/constitutive simplifications, surrogate approximation, lack of patient outcomes) and outline concrete next steps to address them.
must_not_claim: That these limitations invalidate the core sensitivity findings
That future work is guaranteed to change the directional conclusions (material dominance) without further evidence

paragraphs.heading: Clinical importance of plaque rupture
paragraphs.purpose: State the clinical burden: coronary atherosclerotic plaque rupture causes acute coronary syndromes (ACS) and a large share of cardiovascular mortality, motivating improved rupture-risk metrics.
must_not_claim: Novel computational contributions or results from this study (methods/results belong later).
Any new clinical trial evidence or patient-outcome validation.

paragraphs.purpose: Summarize mechanistic determinants of rupture risk (morphology, hemodynamics, material strength) and explain that these factors interact to set vulnerability.
must_not_claim: That any single factor is universally dominant (quantitative dominance is a study result).

paragraphs.heading: Limitations of stress-only metrics and role of strength
paragraphs.purpose: Explain the conceptual limitation of prior computational VI definitions that use stress-only metrics and fixed cap-strength constants, argue why a stress/strength ratio is a more physically meaningful metric, and cite prior literature noting stress/strength concerns.
must_not_claim: Empirical proof that stress/strength outperforms stress-only metrics (this is a result shown later).
That the particular normalization exponent α is definitively correct (discussion later).

paragraphs.heading: Need for simultaneous, pulsatile FSI exploration
paragraphs.purpose: Argue that identifying which factor group (morphology/hemodynamics/materials) dominates VI requires varying all three over a wide, realistic space under pulsatile (time-resolved) FSI — but high computational cost has prevented such studies.
must_not_claim: That previous studies have attempted and failed with identical experimental designs (only state the general high-cost limitation).
Methodological details or validation of the cost-effective FSI (those belong to Methods).

paragraphs.heading: Study objective and approach
paragraphs.purpose: State the study aim: using a previously validated cost-effective pulsatile FSI pipeline to generate a large design-space dataset for two idealized plaque phenotypes, define stress/strength VIs (including ΔPSS-based stress and E_fc^α strength normalization), select clinically consistent VIs, and quantify global sensitivity via GPR surrogates + Sobol to determine dominant factor groups.
must_not_claim: Novelty or validation of the cost-effective FSI method itself (out_of_scope — cite only).
Final quantitative results (these belong in Results).

paragraphs.heading: Summary of main findings
paragraphs.purpose: Concisely restate the study's principal contributions: definition and selection of stress/strength VIs, superiority of ΔPSS as the stress metric, and material-property dominance identified by surrogate Sobol analysis.
must_not_claim: Do not claim clinical validation on patient outcomes
Do not claim that VIs are proven clinical diagnostic tools beyond surrogate-based synthetic-label evaluation
Do not assert novelty or validation of the cost-effective FSI solver itself

paragraphs.heading: Implications for modelling and clinical risk stratification
paragraphs.purpose: State the practical implications: need for pulsatile FSI when assessing fatigue-driven rupture risk, necessity of strength-normalization (E_fc^α), and that material-property characterization (e.g., vessel and cap stiffness) should be prioritized for improved risk stratification.
must_not_claim: Do not claim direct patient-level diagnostic superiority over established clinical tests
Do not imply that measuring all material properties is currently trivial or routinely available clinically
Do not assert causation between any single parameter and actual clinical rupture events

paragraphs.heading: Limitations and future work
paragraphs.purpose: Acknowledge study limitations that bound interpretation and specify concrete next steps (patient-specific geometry/data, richer material models, clinical outcome validation, and surrogate-refinement) to translate findings toward clinical applicability.
must_not_claim: Do not claim that these limitations invalidate the central findings
Do not claim completed clinical validation or prospective utility without evidence
Do not claim that the surrogate-based Sobol results exactly equal direct repeated FSI evaluations (acknowledge approximation)

paragraphs.heading: Background and clinical significance
paragraphs.purpose: State the clinical importance of coronary plaque rupture and motivate why quantitative vulnerability assessment is needed.
